correctness.rationale: Boundary Poisson speed is exact. Parseval and geometric-series summation yield (4)-(5). Strict angular monotonicity forces opposite zeros; one strictly increasing scalar function crosses the necessary radial level exactly once on (0,r), proving global optimality and all equality cases. Formal coefficient matching and an implicit-function argument prove the small-radius expansion; the limiting quadratic yields the golden-ratio endpoint. Diagnostic tests supplement, rather than replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Minimizing mean-square nonuniformity of a degree-two circle covering while fixing the geometric obstruction from its farthest interior zero is a natural shape-distortion problem. The result determines a unique asymmetric antipodal companion at every radius and an unexpected golden-ratio asymptotic, establishing a sharp nontrivial benchmark instead of recomputing a known variance without constraints.
